Steve and the Puppet

By: Este de Klerk | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
How many comments like those made by Steve Hofmeyr recently on Twitter can South Africa endure in its current political environment? Was comedian Conrad Koch at liberty to take him on?

Summary:
How many comments like those made by Steve Hofmeyr recently on Twitter can South Africa endure in its current political environment? Was comedian Conrad Koch at liberty to take him on or was it all much ado about nothing?

Hofmeyr recently tweeted that black people are the architects of Apartheid and this caused a fight between him and comedian Conrad Koch on Twitter.

Hofmeyr got a protection order against Koch for "harassing" him and the court order states that Koch (or puppet Chester Missing) may not mention Hofmeyr's name, his sponsors or his business partners directly or indirectly on TV, social media and radio interviews.

Koch will challenge the order in court next Thursday - but it didn't prevent puppet Chester Missing from Tweeting: "It's like we dealing with the racist version of Lord Voldemort from Harry Potter here: he who shall not be named."



Further information:
Hofmeyr obtained an order preventing Koch from making any public statements about him after some of his sponsors admitted the're now considering cancelling his contracts.

The court order prevents Koch from mentioning Hofmeyr's name, even though puppet Chester plays a big role in the political satire show, Late Night News with Loyiso Gola. Chester may not make reference or poke at Hofmeyr.

Koch described Hofmeyr as a racist after Hofmeyr's tweet that black people are the architects of apartheid.

It is not the first time the singer has been cast in the limelight for his apparent racism and supposed white supremist attitude. Earlier this year, he was criticised for singing the old South African anthem at an Afrikaans club in Australia.

In 2012, Hofmeyr made death threats against comedian John Vismas via twitter. He told reporters that he had stood up at the Comedy Central Roast and tweeted that the only reason he didn't "bliksem" the "tasteless" roaster was because Vismas was "too short to hit and it would have ruined the evening for Comedy Central."

In another incident in 2011, Hofmeyr released the lyrics of a song which included the banned k-word. The song titled, "Ons sal dit oorleef", is apparently dedicated to the late leader of the Afrikaner Weerstandsbeweging, Eugene Terre'Blanche, who was killed on his farm in 2010.

Press Release:


Steve Hofmeyr in hot water
He’s been referred to as an “Afrikaner leader by default”. Singer Steve Hofmeyr is in the spotlight yet again following a Tweet that sparked a racial storm on social media. Hofmeyr has been accused of being a racist and a peddler of ignorance and has been forced to return a sponsored vehicle. Are Steve and his detractors simply enjoying freedom of speech or abusing this right? Carte Blanche investigates.


Script:


STEVE & THE PUPPET

PRODUCER: ESTE DE KLERK

ANNOUNCER VOICE: Let’s get ready to rumble: Hofmeyr vs Missing…

Steve Hofmeyr: Afrikaans singer, actor; pro-Afrikaans activist; also known for controversial statements…

Chester Missing: South Africa’s most famous puppet; taking digs at politicians; and political commentator…

ANNOUNCER VOICE: Hofmeyr vs Missing in the #puppetcase.

But, there are also wingmen: on Hofmeyr’s side – Afrikaner activist, Dan Roodt and on Chester Missing’s side - his ventriloquist Conrad Koch.

CHESTER: Where are we?

CONRAD KOCH: We’re here at the Randburg Magistrate’s Court.

CHESTER: Why?

CONRAD KOCH: Because you got a harassment thing.

CHESTER: Were you harassing someone?

CONRAD KOCH: No, you were.

CHESTER: When?

CONRAD KOCH: On twitter.

CHESTER: I don’t know what you write on my… I don’t write my tweets!

DAN ROODT: The statements that Mr Conrad Koch was making were damaging Steve.

An extreme twitter war between Koch & Missing and Hofmeyr, sparked by one controversial tweet from Hofmeyr, lead to the court case.

The tweet on October 23rd said: “Sorry to offend but in my books blacks were the architects of Apartheid. Go figure.”

In response, Koch & Missing launched a civil campaign against Hofmeyr’s racism that publicly ridiculed and denounced Hofmeyr’s views.

DEVI: Is Steve racist?

DAN ROODT: No

DEVI: Are you a racist?

DAN ROODT: I’m not racist and neither is he and we reject utterly that label.

Koch also asked why sponsors associated with Hofmeyr were still supporting him, especially targeting those of the annual festival Afrikaans Is Groot where Steve performed with some of South Africa’s biggest Afrikaans stars.

STEVE HOFMEYR SINGING: Ek sal my woorde wil uitbassuin….

This irked Hofmeyr so much that he ran to court seeking an interim protection order against Chester Missing that was granted on the 10th of November. It prohibited Missing (and Koch) from harassing Hofmeyr, contacting his sponsors, making defamatory statements against him and tagging him on social media.

But - it was game on as Koch & Missing challenged the interim order this week and had it set aside with costs.

DAN ROODT: The R-word, the racist word – This is like a sort of a superstitious magical spell - you cast a spell on someone - as in Harry Potter. Once you call somebody a racist you cast a spell on them and then he freezes up.

DEVI LINK: Steve Hofmeyr is one of South Africa’s most outspoken artists, but he did not want to talk to Carte Blanche.

CHESTER: Now, I want to chat to Devi. Is Devi here? Devi! Is this Carte Blanche?

CONRAD KOCH: Yes, it is.

LOUIS: Hi Chester!

CHESTER: Who is this? Hello, what is your name?

LOUIS: Hello, how are you? I am Louis.

CHESTER: Hello Louis. How’s it Louis? I like her earrings!

LOUIS: Oh, thanks!

CHESTER: It’s huge, man! They look like they came from Nkandla!

CONRAD: I know! Chester, what are you here for?

CHESTER: I want to speak to Devi, man.

CONRAD: Why?

CHESTER: Because I am the first puppet to be sued and to have won. I have also won!

CONRAD: He got sued and he won, he is on a big ego-trip.

CHESTER: It is not an ego-trip! I’m the first puppet in the whole world! Is Devi here?

LOUIS: Yes, Devi is here.

CHESTER: I want to talk to her.

LOUIS; Let me call her.

CHESTER: Thank you! Devi!!!!

LOUIS: Hello, Devi? Chester is here to see you.

CHESTER: Thanks!

DEVI: Hellloooo! Are you going to tell me about it? Are YOU going to tell me about it?

CHESTER: Yes, yes, I can say anything! Steve Hofmeyr!

DEVI: Come. So you knew what you were saying the minute you responded?

CONRAD: Our first response was, he said: “In his book blacks are the architects of apartheid…” and Chester’s reply was, what did you say?

CHESTER: Yes, because you haven’t graduated from the books that you coloured in yet.

CONRAD: Chester’s humorous response and then Steve said: no, but you can’t proof that it is racist. Denying the atrocities of apartheid creates a structural dynamic where we are accepting of racist views which moves the entire discussion right. It makes the atrocities of apartheid, we are still struggling with our history – the ramifications – people are still living in extreme poverty, it makes it legitimate because we have accepted these views and if you don’t speak up, then no-one ever counters it in the cultural discussion.

DEVI LINK: Freedom of expression is a highly debated topic in South Africa, but it is enshrined in our Constitution. So, what happens when freedom of expression is interpreted as racism?

ADAM HABIB: I think its wonderful that we could have a in the persona of a puppet become the advocate for free speech in our society.

Political analyst Adam Habib says the questions that need to be asked is why people still go to Hofmeyr’s concerts and why sponsors are still supporting him?

ADAM HABIB: I would like others who associate with Steve Hofmeyr to stand up and say: “Excuse me, I find your remarks offensive. In fact, I am not going to attend your concerts or corporates should say we are not going to have you as a mascot, because I promise you let that happen and you watch how quickly Steve Hofmeyr becomes a nonracial advocate.

TIM DU PLESSIS: Steve is very well-known and I think he gets some gratification from the fact that he gets South Africans talking and moving and agitating across the board.

Leading Afrikaans editor and columnist, Tim du Plessis says Steve is not the “Afrikaner leader by default”.

TIM DU PLESSIS: Many Afrikaans people are saying Steve is not speaking on behalf of all of us.

DEVI: Do you think it’s a personal vendetta against Steve?

DAN: I would even say that he was jealous of him, because even though he has got his puppet and so on, I don’t think that the public at large has the same warm feeling about him.

CONRAD: If that was true, then I definitely need to be sued by Jacob Zuma and Helen Zille and Julius Malema, because I have been way meaner to them. It’s got to do with power, the people who accept him and at the same time the corporate who sponsor him. Those two combined makes this one of the most racist moments I’ve ever seen in my history as a satarist.

ADAM HABIB: Do I think Steve Hofmeyr is taken seriously by mainstream South Africans? No. But does he have the capacity to inflame passions in the wrong circumstances? Absolutely.

And so, Chester and Conrad found themselves in court. Thursday this week was D-day in the “puppetcase”. Chester arrived at court dressed in a suit and red tie and he told us he’d borrowed it from his good friend, Pinnochio.

CHESTER: Where are these guys from?

CONRAD: They are from TV. That is Carte Blanche and that is E-tv.

CHESTER: Ok, ok. Carte Blanche? Are they still running?

CONRAD: Yes, they’re still running.

Dan Roodt arrived on his own to represent Hofmeyr who couldn’t make it, having been in Cape Town for the Afrikaans Is Groot concerts there.

CONRAD: We gonna get through security…

CHESTER: So, let’s go!

CONRAD: But you got to go on the machine.

CHESTER: No, hang on! I’m not a thing!

Once inside, Chester did what he does best – soliciting some laughs while speaking to the media – after all he is the first puppet to ever appear in court – taking up the front row seat nogals!

CHESTER: Viva, lawyers, viva!

Roodt, who is not a lawyer, argued in court that Koch and Missing was attacking and defaming Hofmeyr as a person and that Hofmeyr is a member of the minority.

DEVI: Did Steve not insult though an entire group of people by saying that they were architects of apartheid the very system that compromised their lives?

DAN: Possibly he did, but a group of people cannot be insulted to the same extent as an individual.

DEVI: Why?

DAN: Because, I mean, it’s a whole mass of people and not everybody in that mass feels insulted by it.

Koch’s legal team argued that Hofmeyr is a public figure and that through his public and robust advocacy of racism, he has invited a robust response.

DARIO: One thing that is very important is that what Chester Missing was not saying is I want to censor Steve’s views. In fact, that’s what Steve did. He censored the puppet’s views.

Magistrate Naren Sewnarain set the interim protection order aside with punitive costs. He ruled that Hofmeyr exposed himself to criticism and satire by making racially provocative statements.

DARIO: It was regarded as an abuse of process by the magistrate and he said that it was fixacious and unreasonable for Steve Hofmeyr and Dan Roodt to have brought this action under this piece of legislation.

But somehow it seemed that not everyone was happy with the judgment. Outside court Dan Roodt attacked Chester.

DAN ROODT: Die boere is hier om te bly! And we are never going to leave this country!

TIM DU PLESSIS: Because of the involvement of Dan Roodt, I often wonder, you know, shouldn’t one ask whether you get the absurdity of this whole situation?

After the judgment, Hofmeyr tweeted that the setting aside of the interim protection order signalled the end of freedom of speech.

ADAM HABIB: I do not believe that we are going to stop racist remarks being made by either Steve Hofmeyr or many others in our society. A society as a collective, through its own social sensibilities, should determine what it thinks is appropriate or not.

metadata.Further information: Hofmeyr obtained an order preventing Koch from making any public statements about him after some of his sponsors admitted the're now considering cancelling his contracts. The court order prevents Koch from mentioning Hofmeyr's name, even though puppet Chester plays a big role in the political satire show, Late Night News with Loyiso Gola. Chester may not make reference or poke at Hofmeyr. Koch described Hofmeyr as a racist after Hofmeyr's tweet that black people are the architects of apartheid. It is not the first time the singer has been cast in the limelight for his apparent racism and supposed white supremist attitude. Earlier this year, he was criticised for singing the old South African anthem at an Afrikaans club in Australia. In 2012, Hofmeyr made death threats against comedian John Vismas via twitter. He told reporters that he had stood up at the Comedy Central Roast and tweeted that the only reason he didn't "bliksem" the "tasteless" roaster was because Vismas was "too short to hit and it would have ruined the evening for Comedy Central." In another incident in 2011, Hofmeyr released the lyrics of a song which included the banned k-word. The song titled, "Ons sal dit oorleef", is apparently dedicated to the late leader of the Afrikaner Weerstandsbeweging, Eugene Terre'Blanche, who was killed on his farm in 2010.
